neet_phy_u01_t05_1.working: The argument kx must be dimensionless, so [k] = 1/[L] = [L^-1].

neet_phy_u01_t05_2.working: New unit of force = 0.1 kg × 0.1 m / s^2 = 0.01 N. So 10 N = 10 / 0.01 = 1000 units.

neet_phy_u01_t05_3.working: a/V^2 has the dimensions of P, so a = PV^2 = [ML^-1T^-2][L^6] = [ML^5T^-2].

neet_phy_u01_t05_4.working: A: ωt is dimensionless, so ω is [T^-1] (I). B: a = PV^2 = [ML^5T^-2] (II). C: bx is dimensionless, so b is [L^-1]; a/b has the dimensions of P, so a = Pb = [ML^-2T^-2] (IV). D: T = 2π√(l/g), so l/g is [T^2] (III).

neet_phy_u01_t05_5.working: A true: dimensionless constants cannot be found. B true: scalar or vector cannot be told. C false: a dimensionally correct equation need not be physically correct. D false: exponential relations cannot be derived. E true: only like dimensions can be added or subtracted. Correct set is A, B and E.
